div.head: Hl 16.2
div.ab: Gif he þæt ne mæge, gekyþe ðanne in wiofode mid his gewitena anum oþþe mid cyninges wicgerefan, þæt he þæt feoh undeornunga his cuþan ceape in wic gebohte; ⁊ him man þanne his weorð agefe.
Gif he þæt ne mæge, gekyþe ðanne in wiofode mid his gewitena anum oþþe mid cyninges wicgerefan, þæt he þæt feoh undeornunga his cuþan ceape in wic gebohte; and him man þanne his weorð agefe.
Gif he þæt ne mæge, gekyþe ðanne in wiofode mid his gewitena anum oþþe mid cyninges wicgerefan þat he þat feoh undeornunga his cuþan ceape in wic gebohte, ⁊ him man þanne his weorð agefe.

Wenn er [der Verklagte] das nicht kann, dann erkläre er am Altar mit einem seiner Zeugen oder mit des Königs Stadtvogte [als seinem Eideshelfer], dass er jene Fahrhabe unverhohlen durch seinen offenkundigen Kauf in [dieser] Stadt kaufte; und jener [Kläger] gebe ihm dann deren Preis zurück.

If he [the accused] cannot do that, then let him declare at the altar with one of his witnesses or with the king’s town-reeve [as his oath-helper] that he bought those goods openly by his public purchase in [that] town; and let that [plaintiff] then give him back their price.

If he cannot do so, he shall declare on the altar, with one of his witnesses or with the reeve of the king’s estate, that he bought the property openly in London, and with goods known to be his, and the value [of the property] shall be returned to him.

If he cannot do that, he is then to declare at the altar with one of his witnesses or with the king’s town-reeve, that he bought that property openly by a public transaction in the town, and he is then to be given back his price.

If he is unable to do that, let him declare then at the altar with one of his witnesses or with the king’s town-reeve that he bought that property without secrecy by his public purchase in the town; and [the] one [who sold it to him] should then give him back the price of it.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Eidesform 7. Es erhellt nicht, ob die anderen Kaufzeugen ohne Eid dabeistehen, wie o. 5¹⁰, oder gar nicht erscheinen
Cf. Gl Eidesform 7. It is not clear whether the other witnesses to the purchase stand by without swearing, as above 5¹⁰, or do not appear at all
Nicht ‘für sein eigen Geld’, wie Frühere verstanden (property known to be his; Toller Suppl. 136). Der Ggs. ist vielmehr ‘heimlich verstohlener Handel’; s. d. 6. 8e
Not ‘for his own money’, as earlier scholars understood it (property known to be his; Toller Suppl. 136). The contrast is rather ‘secret, furtive trading’; see that word 6. 8e

Der gutgläubige Erwerber erhielt damit besonderen Schutz seines Handels; s. d. Gl 11; hier zuerst wird der Preisersatz ihm zuerkannt; H. Meyer Publizität 75. Dies Privileg sollte vielleicht Käufer zum Londoner Markt locken und Kents Herrschaft in London beliebt machen. Es bezeugt Londons kommerzielle Wichtigkeit; Pol Mai II 157

The purchaser in good faith thereby received special protection for his transaction; see that word in Gl 11; here for the first time reimbursement of the price is awarded to him; H. Meyer Publizität 75. This privilege was perhaps meant to attract buyers to the London market and to make Kent’s rule in London popular. It testifies to London’s commercial importance; Pol Mai II 157
Or perhaps ‘the king’s reeve in London.’
Or rather, perhaps, ‘in a public transaction.’

note.label: transaction
note.seg: or “with goods known to be his” (Attenborough)

note.label: it.
note.seg: Grammatically it is ambiguous as to whether his refers to the owner or the object, but the verb agifan, ‘restore,’ implies that the weorþ, ‘price,’ must be the purchase price rather than a new fine assessed for the damage to the owner’s honour. If his is taken to mean ‘the owner’s,’ the translation would read ‘give him back his [purchase]-price.’ As the next clause discusses the stolen property, it seems more logical to similarly relate his in this clause to the purloined goods. The result would be the same under either reading.
